debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: An open-source CDC engine that reads SQL Server change tables and writes to Kafka topics, one per table.
debezium.bestWhen: Kafka is already in your stack.
debezium.watchOut: after an outage the docs warn of duplicate events, and you run Kafka plus a schema history topic yourself.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run service that documents four ways to find SQL Server changes, including Teleport Sync for when CDC is off.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to run the pipeline and you are fine with row-based billing.
fivetran.watchOut: with CDC it syncs only tables with a single capture instance, so a new column means a new instance.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: An open-source option whose SQL Server connector uses CDC in scheduled syncs, with Iceberg on S3 through its S3 Data Lake destination.
airbyte.bestWhen: scheduled syncs are fine and you want something you can run yourself.
airbyte.watchOut: incremental CDC needs a primary key, delivery is at least once, and its docs do not treat CDC as continuous streaming.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: Three SQL Server connectors: CDC, change tracking and batch, so you can pick per table.
estuary.bestWhen: your tables are a mix, some with keys and some without.
estuary.watchOut: the CDC worker must run on the primary, and its platform uses the Business Source License.

striim.name: Striim
striim.summary: Two readers: MS SQL Reader for CDC tables and MSJet for log backups, which has lower use of the source server.
striim.bestWhen: source load is your main worry and you run big, busy servers.
striim.watchOut: its Iceberg writers cover Google Cloud Storage or Amazon S3 Tables, not plain S3.

fabric.name: Microsoft Fabric mirroring
fabric.summary: Microsoft's own way to copy a SQL Server database into Fabric.
fabric.bestWhen: Fabric is where your analysts work.
fabric.watchOut: data lands in Fabric OneLake as Delta tables, and a schema change breaks mirroring on 2016 to 2022 until you re-enable CDC for the table.

olake.name: OLake Go (ours)
olake.summary: Our open-source tool. Per its docs it reads SQL Server CDC capture instances (2017 or later) and writes Apache Iceberg or Parquet.
olake.bestWhen: you want SQL Server changes in Iceberg tables on storage you own and can run a container.
olake.watchOut: it writes Iceberg and Parquet, you run it on your own infrastructure, and CDC needs to be enabled on each table first.
